## Problem

context-mode spawns one MCP server process per agent session (stdio). For users running many concurrent sessions (T3 Code threads, parallel agent fleets), RAM scales with sessions × server size:

- Our machine: **4 instances for 2 active threads, 32–66 MB each** (2026-11-06).
- A practitioner report of the same plugin family's fix: a stateless Streamable HTTP daemon cut **36 processes / 2.2 GB → 1 process / ~80 MB**, flat as sessions were added (systemd user unit, loopback + auth).

Claude Code itself has no stdio sharing yet — anthropics/claude-code#63251 and anthropics/claude-code#107433 are open feature requests, and anthropics/claude-code#103693 documents 91 copies of one server totaling 5.7 GB. A server-side shared mode would fix the multiplier for every affected host, independent of client-side sharing.

## Request

An opt-in **stateless shared daemon mode**:

- One process per machine (or per project database), serving all sessions over loopback **Streamable HTTP**.
- **Stateless request handling**: session state (per-project SQLite index, session continuity keys) is keyed per request/session id, never held in process-global mutable state — so any request can be served by the one process safely, and a restart loses nothing the index does not already hold.
- Documented `systemd` user unit (loopback bind, `Restart=on-failure`) like the practitioner pattern above.
- An install-time switch (e.g. `context-mode setup --daemon`) that rewrites the MCP registration from a stdio spawn to an HTTP URL, plus `/ctx-doctor` checks for daemon reachability.

The v2 rewrite's "one database per project" model fits this well: the daemon's contention surface is SQLite, which already handles concurrent readers.

## Verification

- N concurrent sessions → exactly one context-mode process (`ps`), RSS flat in N.
- `ctx_search` returns indexed content from all sessions; sandboxed execution and session continuity behave as per-session spawns do.
